rows.name: enemy sprite layout table
rows.notes: PRG ROM table that says which sprite-pattern-table (CHR $0000) tile ids make up each enemy's metasprite, one entry per enemy/frame. Each entry is 6 bytes: the first two are the metasprite's blank top row (fill tile $FC for a 16x24 enemy such as the Goomba) and the last four are the 2x2 body, drawn as four 8x8 OAM sprites. What the bytes are (Goomba entry at prgRom 0x6792, 6 bytes): FC FC 70 71 72 73 = upper-left $70, upper-right $71, lower-left $72, lower-right $73 (exactly the OAM tile sequence list_sprites decodes for the World 1-1 Goomba). FOUND with no reference: search_memory prgRom for the Goomba's tile ids in draw order - 'FC FC 70 71 72 73' matched uniquely at 0x6792 and '70 71 72 73' uniquely at 0x6794 in the whole 32 KiB PRG. The hit checks out structurally: the neighbouring 6-byte entries are the other enemies' metasprites (0x6798 = FC FC 6E 6E 6F 6F green koopa, 0x679E = FC FC 6D 6D 6F 6F red koopa, 0x67A4/0x67AA = the mirrored frames, 0x67B0-0x67C2 = FC FC F4 F4 F5 F5 / F5 F5 F4 F4 buzzy beetle, 0x67C8 = FC FC FC FC EF EF, 0x67CE = B9 B8 BB BA BC BC, ...). PROOF (ledgered write in the throwaway hack eval-sheet2-d): write_memory prgRom 0x6794 (the Goomba's upper-left tile id) 0x70 -> 0xD6 (fire-flower head graphic, same sprite pattern table), reason recorded, ledger seq 1; reset_emulator (the byte read back $D6 at CPU $E794, so the ROM edit survived), replayed Start/Start to World 1-1, then paused with the first Goomba on screen: list_sprites returned the Goomba's OAM group with tiles 113 ($71), 214 ($D6), 115 ($73), 114 ($72) - the upper-left quadrant swapped from $70 to $D6 while the other three stayed; get_region object mode at (126,198) returned the 16x16 sprite-palette-7 Goomba object across CHR 0x71/0x72/0x73/0xD6 (188 px, box (122,193)-(137,208)). undo_edit seq 1 restored 0x70 (CPU $E794 read back 112,113,114,115). BOUNDING THE TABLE: the Goomba's entry is exactly 6 bytes at 0x6792-0x6797. The run of consecutive 6-byte entries that carry the $FC $FC top-row padding starts at the Goomba entry and continues through 0x67DF (13 entries = 78 bytes: 0x6792, 0x6798, 0x679E, 0x67A4, 0x67AA, 0x67B0, 0x67B6, 0x67BC, 0x67C2, 0x67C8, 0x67CE, 0x67D4, 0x67DA); at 0x67E0 the 6-byte entries stop carrying the $FC $FC padding (0x67E0 begins CD CD CE CE CF CF ...), so 0x6792..0x67DF is the padded run I can bound. The table's absolute first and last byte were NOT pinned to an indexing routine (read-tracing the ROM range in this bridge returned no reads), so I do not claim a larger length than the padded run.
